topics.topic: Exact rule for recognizing Syncthing conflict copies
questions: By what exact rule does the deliverer determine that a file is a Syncthing conflict copy, including supported Syncthing naming variants and files whose names merely resemble conflict copies?
By what exact, testable rule does the deliverer distinguish a Syncthing conflict copy from an ordinary file?
By what exact, versioned rule does the deliverer recognize a Syncthing conflict copy, including filename pattern, case handling and files in subfolders?

quotes:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).
judgement.why: State 2 defines conflict-copy recognition by a case-insensitive name rule applied at every path level, including names that merely contain the conflict marker.

topics.topic: How excluded conflict copies are presented in the workplace
questions: Does the workplace hide conflict copies completely, or show them as excluded with a reason so the owner can know which files require renaming?
Does the workplace omit the conflict copy entirely, show it as ineligible with a reason, or report it separately?
Does "does not offer" mean the conflict copy is entirely absent from the workplace, or visible there as excluded with a reason?

quotes:
Ignored names are
not reported, ignored folders are not entered, and symbolic links are neither reported nor followed.

- INV-18: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). A real Syncthing conflict leaves its copy unreported while the photo itself is still reported (`e2e_local_syncthing.py`, `a real Syncthing conflict copy is not offered`).
judgement.why: State 2 says conflict copies are absent from scan results rather than displayed as excluded observations.

topics.topic: Rechecking conflict status before delivery and handling a stale selection
questions: If a file was offered and chosen while ordinary but becomes a Syncthing conflict copy before placement, must the calling flow reclassify it, and what result does it report?
Must conflict status be checked again after listing and before placing, and what result is reported if a selected ordinary file becomes a conflict copy before delivery?

If a selected ordinary photo becomes or is replaced by a conflict copy after it was offered but before placement or publication, must the calling flow reject it, or may it complete the selected delivery?

quotes: - INV-18: a Syncthing conflict copy is neither reported by a scan nor placed.

- INV-18: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). A real Syncthing conflict leaves its copy unreported while the photo itself is still reported (`e2e_local_syncthing.py`, `a real Syncthing conflict copy is not offered`).

3. Inside the call the folder is scanned once. A requested source with no placement that this scan
   does not report as `ready` fails with `not_ready_or_absent`. A source reported `ready` whose
   bytes no longer have the requested hash when it is read for placing fails with `source_changed`.

1. The calling flow publishes a placed photo, then records the Portal `photo_id` at the deliverer
   (R0-08). It does not publish an item reported as `published`, or a replayed placement that
   carries a `photo_id`.
judgement.why: State 2 requires a fresh scan inside placement, rejects an already-conflicting selected source as `not_ready_or_absent`, detects later content change as `source_changed`, and publishes without rechecking the source only after placement has succeeded.

topics.topic: Rename required to make a conflict copy ordinary and when it becomes offerable
questions: What exact rename makes an excluded conflict copy ordinary: any rename event, or only a resulting name that no longer matches the conflict-copy rule?
When does the deliverer observe the rename and make the file eligible to appear among ready photos?
What rename makes the file ordinary, when is that change detected, and does it become offerable subject to the existing content-delivery rule or regardless of prior delivery of identical content?
What exact rename makes the file ordinary, and when must the renamed file become eligible for the ready-photo list?

quotes:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).
- Continuity: Nothing continues between scans; the next scan observes the folder again.

A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status. The first rule that
applies decides:

| Order | Condition | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | its age is below the settling time, which includes a modification time in the future | `settling` | none |
| 2 | empty | `rejected` | `empty` |
| 3 | larger than the source limit | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 4 | when opened it is no longer a regular file | `rejected` | `not_a_regular_file` |
| 5 | it grew past the source limit while being read | `rejected` | `too_large` |
| 6 | opening or reading it fails, including a file that disappeared or became a link | `rejected` | `unreadable_file` |
| 7 | does not begin with a JPEG, PNG or WEBP signature | `rejected` | `unsupported_format` |
| 8 | same content as an earlier file of this scan | `duplicate` | `duplicate_content`, with `duplicate_of` |
| 9 | placed and marked | `published` | none |
| 10 | placed | `placed` | none |
| 11 | anything else | `ready` | none |
1. A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).
judgement.why: State 2 makes eligibility depend on the resulting filename at the next on-demand scan, and ordinary-file status still follows content identity, so previously placed identical content is not newly ready.

topics.topic: Migration of existing deliverer state when conflict-copy exclusion takes effect
questions: When R0-14 takes effect, what happens to conflict copies already cached as ready, previously selected, or stored in deliverer records?

quotes: - Continuity: Nothing continues between scans; the next scan observes the folder again.

- INV-18: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). A real Syncthing conflict leaves its copy unreported while the photo itself is still reported (`e2e_local_syncthing.py`, `a real Syncthing conflict copy is not offered`).

2. Placing an existing placement answers `replayed` with the stored placement and the current
   `photo_id` of its mark, if any, and writes nothing, even when the source file has left the
   folder.

7. The first version offers no removal of a placement, a mark or a stored image. Removal of a
   hidden photo is designed in the Portal (client-portal Q27).
judgement.why: State 2 has no persistent ready cache, reclassifies unplaced selections on the next placement scan, and retains existing placement and publication records for replay rather than migrating or deleting them.
